title: checkForPlaintextSecret: add high-entropy detection for real tokens (bi-directional check)
description:
The checkForPlaintextSecret function in packages/types/src/types/secret-detection.ts currently warns when entropy is low (< 3.8) — catching human-readable plaintext passwords stored in integration auth YAML fields.

However, there are two distinct threat classes that one threshold can't catch:
- Low entropy (< 3.8): human-readable passwords like "password123"
- High entropy (> 4.5): real cryptographic tokens like JWTs, bearer tokens, API keys stored directly in YAML

The current check only catches the first class. A JWT stored as `token: "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9..."` passes through silently.

Suggested fix: change the condition to `entropy < 3.8 || entropy > 4.5` to catch both classes. Update the warning message to distinguish which case triggered.

Additional context: checkForPlaintextSecret is currently exported but never called (dead code). This issue should also cover wiring it into the prebuild pipeline at the integration auth processing point in packages/build-scripts/src/prebuild.ts. Consider adding a minimum length guard (e.g., skip values < 32 chars for the high-entropy check) to reduce false positives from short but random-looking strings.

title: refactor(cli): replace gh CLI in git open-pr with generic git push
description:
The `stackwright git open-pr` command in packages/cli/src/commands/git-ops.ts uses the `gh` CLI for two things: (1) `gh pr create` to open a pull request, and (2) the shared `gh()` utility in utils/git.ts. This creates a hard dependency on GitHub and the gh CLI for what is fundamentally a content publishing workflow.

Proposed replacement:
- Replace `gh pr create` with a plain `git push` followed by a printed URL hint or provider-detected PR link (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea all support opening PRs from a push URL)
- Remove the `gh()` utility from utils/git.ts once it has no remaining callers
- Update the `stackwright_open_pr` MCP tool description accordingly

This unblocks citizen developers using Gitea, Codeberg, GitLab, or any other git host.
